transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

Well, I came in because I just... I keep getting these awful, unwanted thoughts that I’ve missed something critical. Like, at work, I do a lot of data analysis, and I'll be convinced I left a wrong number in a data release. Which is funny because my boss, Richard, he's actually the one who usually messes up the spreadsheets. He’s been at the company for fifteen years and still doesn't know how to use pivot tables. I actually had to show him twice last month, and he always brings in these stale donuts from the gas station to apologize. 

But anyway, it’s not just work. It’s things like... being terrified I left the back door unlocked, or that I paid a bill from the wrong account. I just switched to that new credit union down on 4th street, actually, because my old bank had terrible customer service—I was on hold for two hours once just to ask about a routing fee, and they played that same classical music loop over and over. 

But... where was I? Right, the thoughts. Even when I know I checked the door, or the numbers, or the account, my mind just won’t let go of the possibility that I’ve caused some sort of huge disaster. It just won't stop.

Do you find yourself doing certain things over and over again, like checking, counting, or repeating actions in your mind, to try to make those worries go away or prevent something bad from happening?

Oh, definitely. I mean, to calm myself down when I get like that, I end up reopening the spreadsheets over and over. Which is honestly a nightmare because our company uses this incredibly outdated version of Excel, and it takes forever to load on my laptop. The IT guy, Kevin, keeps promising he’ll upgrade my machine, but he’s always "busy" playing some computer game in his office. I literally saw him playing it when I went down there last Tuesday to ask for a new mousepad. 

But anyway, yeah, I reopen the files, and I reread my emails line by line. And at home, it's the locks, or the payment confirmations. I have to check them over and over in this very specific set order until it finally feels... safe, you know? Like the front door, the back door, the banking app... 

Speaking of the app, that new credit union I mentioned? Their mobile app is so clunky. The font is absolutely tiny. I actually had to buy new reading glasses just to see the transaction numbers. I got these cute tortoiseshell frames from LensCrafters, though they were a bit overpriced if you ask me, and the lady who fitted them was chewing gum so loudly... wait, what was I saying? 

Oh, right, the checking. Because I have to do all that checking in that exact order until my brain accepts that it's safe, some nights I’m still just sitting at my desk hours later, and I haven't actually finished a single thing.
